top_papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
top_papers.key_finding: De novo variants in TCF7L2 are associated with a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delays, mild intellectual disability, and other clinical features, highlighting TCF7L2's role in neurodevelopment.

top_papers.title: N-Acetylglucosamine Kinase-Small Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein Polypeptide N Interaction Promotes Axodendritic Branching in Neurons via Dynein-Mediated Microtubule Transport.
top_papers.key_finding: The interaction between N-acetylglucosamine kinase (NAGK) and SNRPN promotes axodendritic branching and neuronal complexity via dynein-mediated microtubule transport, and this interaction rescues impaired neurodevelopment in SNRPN-depleted neurons derived from Prader-Willi syndrome patient iPSCs.

top_papers.title: Abnormal DNA methylation in pluripotent stem cells from a patient with Prader-Willi syndrome results in neuronal differentiation defects.
top_papers.key_finding: Abnormal methylation of the SNRPN gene in pluripotent stem cells from a Prader-Willi syndrome patient leads to defects in neuronal differentiation, resulting in fewer neural stem cells and mature neurons.

top_papers.title: The autism-related gene SNRPN regulates cortical and spine development via controlling nuclear receptor Nr4a1.
top_papers.key_finding: SNRPN regulates cortical and spine development by controlling the nuclear receptor Nr4a1; both overexpression and knockdown of SNRPN impair neurite outgrowth and neuron migration, with Nr4a1 co-expression rescuing these defects.

top_papers.title: Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein associated polypeptide N accelerates cell proliferation in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
top_papers.key_finding: Knockdown of SNRPN in pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells reduces proliferation, colony formation, and induces S phase arrest and apoptosis, indicating SNRPN's role in cancer cell growth.

top_papers.title: Effect of small nuclear ribonucleoprotein-associated polypeptide N on the proliferation of medulloblastoma cells.
top_papers.key_finding: Silencing SNRPN in medulloblastoma cells significantly reduces proliferation and colony formation, and alters cell cycle distribution, suggesting SNRPN as a potential therapeutic target.

top_papers.title: Case Report: Hypomyelinating Leukodystrophy Type 20 (HLD20) With Novel CNP Gene Variant.
top_papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
top_papers.key_finding: Identified a novel homozygous variant in the CNP gene associated with hypomyelinating leukodystrophy type 20 (HLD20) and showed decreased CNP mRNA expression in patient samples, expanding the genetic and clinical spectrum of HLD20.

top_papers.title: Nanobodies against the myelin enzyme CNPase as tools for structural and functional studies.
top_papers.key_finding: Developed nanobodies against the CNPase enzyme for structural and functional studies, revealing distinct epitopes and inhibitory effects, and demonstrated their utility in imaging and as intrabodies in oligodendrocytes.

top_papers.title: C-type natriuretic peptide as mediator of growth in the absence of growth hormone: Unraveling the mystery of the growth without GH syndrome.
top_papers.key_finding: Discussed the role of C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) as a compensatory growth mediator in the absence of growth hormone, promoting chondrocyte proliferation and hypertrophy, potentially explaining growth without GH syndrome.

top_papers.title: C-type natriuretic peptide attenuates enhanced glycolysis and de novo pyrimidine synthesis in pericytes of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
top_papers.key_finding: Showed that CNP attenuates enhanced glycolysis and de novo pyrimidine synthesis in pericytes from pulmonary arterial hypertension patients via cGMP-dependent kinase I activation, reducing HIF-1α and GLUT-1 expression.

top_papers.title: The CNP analogue vosoritide mediates PDE2-sensitive anti-arrhythmogenic effects in mouse hearts with STZ-induced type 1 diabetes.
top_papers.key_finding: Demonstrated that the CNP analogue vosoritide mediates PDE2-sensitive anti-arrhythmogenic effects in diabetic mouse hearts, reducing arrhythmia incidence after ischemia-reperfusion injury.

top_papers.title: Functional analysis and verification of GYG2 in oncolytic virus-infected glioma.
top_papers.key_finding: This study directly investigates GYG2 in glioma cells infected with oncolytic viruses, showing GYG2 downregulation after infection and its association with glioma clinical features, survival, and tumor microenvironment, with functional experiments demonstrating GYG2's role in glioma cell growth and apoptosis.

top_papers.title: Human glycogenins maintain glucose homeostasis by regulating glycogen metabolism.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper elucidates distinct physiological roles of human glycogenins GYG1 and GYG2 in glycogen synthesis, demonstrating that GYG2 acts as a suppressor of glycogen formation and regulates glucose homeostasis, providing insights into glycogen metabolism and potential therapeutic implications.

top_papers.title: Transcriptome-wide analysis reveals GYG2 as a mitochondria-related aging biomarker in human subcutaneous adipose tissue.
top_papers.key_finding: GYG2 is identified as a novel mitochondria-related aging biomarker in human subcutaneous adipose tissue, linked to mitochondrial function and brown/beige adipocytes, with PPARG identified as a transcription factor regulating GYG2 expression, suggesting a role in adipose tissue aging mechanisms.

top_papers.title: Glycogen Synthesis in Glycogenin 1-Deficient Patients: A Role for Glycogenin 2 in Muscle.
top_papers.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
top_papers.key_finding: This study shows that in glycogenin-1-deficient patients, glycogenin-2 is present and may compensate for glycogen synthesis in muscle, indicating a role for GYG2 in glycogen metabolism in the absence of GYG1.

top_papers.title: A hemizygous GYG2 mutation and Leigh syndrome: a possible link?
top_papers.key_finding: A hemizygous missense mutation in GYG2 was identified in male siblings with Leigh syndrome, with structural modeling and in vitro experiments showing the mutation disrupts GYG2 self-glucosylation, suggesting a possible link between GYG2 dysfunction and this neurodegenerative disorder.

top_papers.title: A-kinase anchoring protein 17 A promotes hypoxic adaptation and tumor growth by augmenting HIF1α protein synthesis.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A promotes hypoxic adaptation and tumor growth by augmenting HIF1α protein synthesis through a PKA-independent mechanism; AKAP17A depletion reduces HIF1α abundance and tumor proliferation.

top_papers.title: Proteomic analysis reveals CAAP1 negatively correlates with platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A interacts with the splicing factor CAAP1 and is implicated in modulating platinum sensitivity in ovarian cancer cells via mRNA splicing pathways.

top_papers.title: The transcript expression levels of HNRNPM, HNRNPA0 and AKAP17A splicing factors may be predictively associated with ageing phenotypes in human peripheral blood.
top_papers.key_finding: Transcript levels of AKAP17A splicing factor are predictively associated with aging phenotypes, including cognitive decline and physical ability deterioration in human peripheral blood.

top_papers.title: Host Genetic and Gut Microbial Signatures in Familial Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A contains rare, potentially deleterious variants transmitted in familial inflammatory bowel disease, indicating a possible genetic contribution to disease risk.

top_papers.title: Transcriptome profiling of fetal Klinefelter testis tissue reveals a possible involvement of long non-coding RNAs in gonocyte maturation.
top_papers.key_finding: AKAP17A is upregulated in fetal Klinefelter syndrome testis tissue, suggesting a possible involvement in gonocyte maturation and testicular phenotype.

top_papers.title: Vps34-orchestrated lipid signaling processes regulate the transitional heterogeneity and functional adaptation of effector regulatory T cells.
top_papers.key_finding: Genetic deletion of the UVRAG-interacting protein in Tregs revealed that UVRAG is essential for effector regulatory T cell transitional heterogeneity and functional adaptation, highlighting its critical role in immune regulation.

top_papers.title: Ubiquitination of UVRAG by SMURF1 promotes autophagosome maturation and inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma growth.
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG is ubiquitinated by SMURF1 promoting autophagosome maturation and inhibiting hepatocellular carcinoma growth; deubiquitination by ZRANB1 reverses this effect, revealing a regulatory mechanism of UVRAG in autophagy and cancer.

top_papers.title: Darkening with UVRAG.
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG has a specialized function in melanosome biogenesis beyond autophagy through interaction with BLOC-1, regulated by MITF and α-MSH signaling, influencing skin pigmentation and melanoma predisposition.

top_papers.title: Central role of autophagic UVRAG in melanogenesis and the suntan response.
top_papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG plays a central role in melanogenesis and the suntan response by interacting with BLOC-1, required for melanosome biogenesis and melanocyte development, acting as a direct target of MITF.

top_papers.title: A critical role for UVRAG in apoptosis.
top_papers.key_finding: UVRAG has anti-apoptotic activity by inhibiting Bax translocation to mitochondria during apoptosis in tumor cells, in addition to its role in autophagy and autophagosome maturation.

top_papers.title: COL11A1 Inhibits Ferroptosis in Pancreatic Cancer by Regulating AKT/Beclin 1 Dependent Autophagy.
top_papers.key_finding: COL11A1 is overexpressed in pancreatic cancer and inhibits ferroptosis by regulating AKT/Beclin 1 dependent autophagy, promoting cancer cell viability and chemoresistance.

top_papers.title: DDR2-COL11A1 Transcriptional Coupling as a Candidate Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer: Integrative Transcriptomic and Deep Learning Validation.
top_papers.key_finding: DDR2-COL11A1 transcriptional coupling is dramatically increased in colorectal cancer, suggesting COL11A1 upregulation and transcriptional coordination as a candidate therapeutic target.

top_papers.title: Lactate derived from macrophages drives skin dermal fibroblasts phenotypic remodeling via MCT1-primed histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation in hypertrophic scar.
top_papers.key_finding: Macrophage-derived lactate promotes hypertrophic scar formation by upregulating COL11A1 via MCT1-primed histone lactylation, establishing a positive feedback loop that amplifies fibrosis.

top_papers.title: The FUS/COL11A1/ZEB1 Axis Contributes to the Development of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
top_papers.journal: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology
top_papers.key_finding: The FUS/COL11A1/ZEB1 axis promotes oral squamous cell carcinoma progression by regulating proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

top_papers.title: Unlocking cellular plasticity: enhancing human iPSC reprogramming through bromodomain inhibition and extracellular matrix gene expression regulation.
top_papers.key_finding: COL11A1 acts as a reprogramming barrier in human iPSC formation; its knockdown enhances reprogramming efficiency by modulating extracellular matrix gene expression and cellular plasticity.

top_papers.title: HDHD1, which is often deleted in X-linked ichthyosis, encodes a pseudouridine-5'-phosphatase.
top_papers.key_finding: This study identifies HDHD1 (an alias of PUDP) as encoding a pseudouridine-5'-phosphatase enzyme, characterizing its enzymatic activity and confirming its molecular identity, thus directly investigating the PUDP gene's function.

top_papers.title: X chromosome dosage and the genetic impact across human tissues.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper analyzes X chromosome gene expression and methylation patterns across tissues, identifying genes with unexpected expression patterns; it likely includes PUDP given its X chromosome location, but PUDP is not the main focus.

top_papers.title: No title
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions X-linked ichthyosis, a condition related to deletions in the X chromosome region where PUDP is located; however, no detailed study of PUDP gene itself is provided.

top_papers.title: Novel Microdeletion in the X Chromosome Leads to Kallmann Syndrome, Ichthyosis, Obesity, and Strabismus.
top_papers.key_finding: Reports a novel microdeletion in Xp22.3 region containing multiple genes; PUDP may be within this region but the paper focuses on contiguous gene syndromes rather than PUDP specifically.

top_papers.title: Genome-wide association analysis of treatment resistant schizophrenia for variant discovery and polygenic assessment.
top_papers.key_finding: No specific mention or study of PUDP gene; focuses on genome-wide association in schizophrenia treatment response.

top_papers.title: Alteration of colonic epithelial cell differentiation in mice deficient for glucosaminyl N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase 4.
top_papers.key_finding: Generated Ndst4 knockout mice showing altered colonic epithelial cell differentiation, supporting NDST4's role as a putative tumor suppressor and its involvement in colon homeostasis.

top_papers.title: NDST4 is a novel candidate tumor suppressor gene at chromosome 4q26 and its genetic loss predicts adverse prognosis in colorectal cancer.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified NDST4 as a novel candidate tumor suppressor gene at chromosome 4q26 with marked downregulation in colorectal cancer tumors, and allelic loss of NDST4 predicts adverse prognosis.

top_papers.title: Characterization of heparan sulfate N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase isoform 4 using synthetic oligosaccharide substrates.
top_papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
top_papers.key_finding: Characterized recombinant NDST4 enzyme showing it has N-sulfotransferase activity but lacks N-deacetylase activity, suggesting NDST4 alone does not regulate N-S and N-Ac domain distribution in heparan sulfate biosynthesis.

top_papers.title: Multiple isozymes of heparan sulfate/heparin GlcNAc N-deacetylase/GlcN N-sulfotransferase. Structure and activity of the fourth member, NDST4.
top_papers.key_finding: Cloned and partially characterized NDST4, revealing its sequence similarity to other NDST family members and distinct enzymatic properties, with restricted tissue expression compared to NDST1 and NDST2.

top_papers.title: Genome-wide association study of shared components of reading disability and language impairment.
top_papers.key_finding: Reported genome-wide association of NDST4 markers with language impairment, suggesting a genetic link though NDST4 was not the primary focus of the study.

top_papers.title: A pseudoautosomal glycosylation disorder prompts the revision of dolichol biosynthesis.
top_papers.key_finding: This study identifies DHRSX as essential for dolichol biosynthesis, revealing a three-step pathway where DHRSX catalyzes the first and third steps, and reports a congenital disorder of glycosylation caused by DHRSX mutations.

top_papers.title: Absence of the dolichol synthesis gene DHRSX leads to N-glycosylation defects in Lec5 and Lec9 Chinese hamster ovary cells.
top_papers.key_finding: The paper demonstrates that absence of DHRSX in glycosylation-deficient CHO cell lines leads to defects in dolichol synthesis and N-glycosylation, and that complementation with human DHRSX restores normal function.

top_papers.title: DHRSX, a novel non-classical secretory protein associated with starvation induced autophagy.
top_papers.key_finding: DHRSX is characterized as a novel non-classical secretory protein that promotes starvation-induced autophagy, with overexpression enhancing autophagy markers and knockdown reducing them.

top_papers.title: X chromosome dosage and the genetic impact across human tissues.
top_papers.key_finding: The study includes DHRSX as an X chromosomal gene with expression patterns influenced by X chromosome dosage across human tissues, suggesting possible functional implications.

top_papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing identifies new candidate genes for nonobstructive azoospermia.
top_papers.key_finding: DHRSX is mentioned among genes associated with nonobstructive azoospermia, identified through whole-genome sequencing as a potential candidate gene for spermatogenetic failure.

top_papers.title: A novel nonsense mutation in the STS gene in a Pakistani family with X-linked recessive ichthyosis: including a very rare case of two homozygous female patients.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified a novel nonsense mutation in the STS gene causing X-linked recessive ichthyosis in a Pakistani family, including rare homozygous female patients, with detailed clinical and genetic characterization of STS loss-of-function mutations.

top_papers.title: Cardiac arrhythmia, developmental delay, epilepsy and ichthyosis due to Xp22.31 deletion: review of literature and case report.
top_papers.key_finding: Reported clinical cases with hemizygous Xp22.31 deletions including the STS gene, linking these deletions to ichthyosis and neurological symptoms, emphasizing the broader phenotypic spectrum of STS gene deletions.

top_papers.title: Novel Microdeletion in the X Chromosome Leads to Kallmann Syndrome, Ichthyosis, Obesity, and Strabismus.
top_papers.key_finding: Described novel microdeletions in Xp22.31 region encompassing the STS gene causing contiguous gene syndromes including X-linked ichthyosis, contributing to understanding molecular mechanisms of STS-related disorders.

top_papers.title: Prenatal diagnosis of sex chromosomal inversion, translocation and deletion.
top_papers.key_finding: Performed prenatal diagnosis revealing complex chromosomal rearrangements including deletion of the STS gene region, highlighting the importance of STS gene in genetic counseling and prenatal diagnostics.

top_papers.title: Nine patients with Xp22.31 microduplication, cognitive deficits, seizures, and talipes anomalies.
top_papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
top_papers.key_finding: Presented a series of patients with Xp22.31 microduplications involving the STS gene, associating these duplications with cognitive deficits and seizures, contributing to phenotype-genotype correlations of STS gene variations.

top_papers.title: PCR assay for the inversion causing severe Hemophilia A and its application.
top_papers.key_finding: Developed a long distance PCR assay targeting F8A1 and related regions to detect gene inversion causing severe Hemophilia A, demonstrating a diagnostic application focused on F8A1 gene structure.

top_papers.title: Multivariate eQTL mapping uncovers functional variation on the X-chromosome associated with complex disease traits.
top_papers.key_finding: Identified a strong eSNP (rs35975601) associated with F8A1 gene expression and linked to a type 1 diabetes risk variant, indicating functional variation affecting F8A1 expression on the X-chromosome.

top_papers.title: Development and characterization of a specific IgG monoclonal antibody toward the Lewis x antigen using splenocytes of Schistosoma mansoni-infected mice.
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions F8A1.1 as a monoclonal antibody name unrelated to the F8A1 gene; the study focuses on Lewis x antigen in Schistosoma mansoni and human cells, not on the F8A1 gene itself.

top_papers.title: Comprehensive evaluation of the PCDHB family in gastric cancer: Prognostic significance, immune infiltration, and experimental validation of PCDHB5's oncogenic role.
top_papers.key_finding: This study directly investigates PCDHB5 in gastric cancer, showing it is upregulated and associated with poor prognosis and immune infiltration; functional experiments validate PCDHB5's oncogenic role.

top_papers.title: Weighted genes associated with the progression of retinoblastoma: Evidence from bioinformatic analysis.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 is mentioned as part of the protocadherin beta family genes associated with retinoblastoma progression in a bioinformatic gene co-expression module, but the focus is broader and not specific to PCDHB5.

top_papers.title: Long noncoding RNA HOTAIR promotes metastasis of renal cell carcinoma by up-regulating histone H3K27 demethylase JMJD3.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 expression is regulated epigenetically via histone methylation changes influenced by lncRNA HOTAIR in renal cell carcinoma, suggesting a role in metastasis regulation.

top_papers.title: Nine differentially expressed genes from a post mortem study and their association with suicidal status in a sample of suicide completers, attempters and controls.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 was one of nine genes differentially expressed in suicide victims' cortex, but associations with suicidal behavior were nominal and did not survive correction.

top_papers.title: Influence of differentially expressed genes from suicide post-mortem study on personality traits as endophenotypes on healthy subjects and suicide attempters.
top_papers.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHB5 SNPs were investigated for influence on personality traits as endophenotypes related to suicide, but findings were limited and not conclusive.

top_papers.title: Variants in the zinc transporter TMEM163 cause a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
top_papers.key_finding: Variants in TMEM163 cause a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with impaired zinc efflux function, reduced myelin gene expression, and oligodendroglial dysfunction, demonstrating TMEM163's critical role in CNS myelination.

top_papers.title: Functional Study of
top_papers.key_finding: De novo TMEM163 variants identified in hypomyelinating leukodystrophy patients alter zinc efflux activity; knockdown in zebrafish causes myelin deficits and locomotor disability, confirming TMEM163's functional role in myelination.

top_papers.title: A zinc transporter, transmembrane protein 163, is critical for the biogenesis of platelet dense granules.
top_papers.key_finding: TMEM163 is identified as a critical zinc transporter required for platelet dense granule biogenesis, with its deficiency causing granule defects and altered zinc accumulation, highlighting its functional importance in lysosome-related organelles.

top_papers.title: TMEM163 Regulates ATP-Gated P2X Receptor and Behavior.
top_papers.key_finding: TMEM163 modulates ATP-gated P2X receptor channel properties and is required for full neuronal P2XR function and pain-related behavior, establishing TMEM163 as a critical functional modulator in vivo.

top_papers.title: Transmembrane 163 (TMEM163) protein effluxes zinc.
top_papers.key_finding: Human TMEM163 functions as a zinc efflux transporter, reducing intracellular zinc levels in cultured cells, and mutations in conserved aspartate residues impair this zinc transport activity.

top_papers.title: Protocadherin alpha 3 inhibits lung squamous cell carcinoma metastasis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHA3 is low expressed in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) cell lines; overexpression of PCDHA3 significantly impairs LUSC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, indicating its inhibitory role in metastasis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

top_papers.title: Novel ultra-rare exonic variants identified in a founder population implicate cadherins in schizophrenia.
top_papers.key_finding: A recurrent case mutation in PCDHA3 was identified in schizophrenia patients, resulting in cytoplasmic aggregates and failure of homophilic interactions on the plasma membrane, implicating PCDHA3 in synaptic abnormalities central to schizophrenia.

top_papers.title: Protocadherin alpha gene cluster variants are potentially associated with short root anomaly in Japanese.
top_papers.key_finding: Four missense variants within the protocadherin alpha gene cluster including PCDHA3 were identified in Japanese patients with short root anomaly, suggesting a potential genetic association of PCDHA3 with this dental phenotype.

top_papers.title: LncRNA-ZXF1 stabilizes P21 expression in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma by inhibiting ubiquitination-mediated degradation and regulating the miR-378a-3p/PCDHA3 axis.
top_papers.key_finding: lncRNA-ZXF1 regulates endometrioid endometrial carcinoma cell proliferation and migration partly by acting as a molecular sponge of miR-378a-3p to regulate PCDHA3 expression, indicating a role of PCDHA3 in tumor suppression.

top_papers.title: A risk scoring model for lung squamous cell carcinoma based on epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related genes: an integrative analysis of prognosis and immune infiltration characteristics.
top_papers.key_finding: PCDHA3 is part of a six-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related prognostic signature in lung squamous cell carcinoma, with its expression contributing to risk stratification and immune infiltration characteristics.

top_papers.title: Celecoxib Enhances Oxidative Muscle Fibre Formation and Improves Muscle Functions Through Prokr1 Activation in Mice.
top_papers.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
top_papers.key_finding: Celecoxib acts as a PROKR1 agonist and enhances oxidative muscle fiber formation and muscle function in mice, demonstrating PROKR1's role in muscle physiology and potential therapeutic applications.

top_papers.title: Prokineticin receptor 1 ameliorates insulin resistance in skeletal muscle.
top_papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
top_papers.key_finding: PROKR1 activation in skeletal muscle improves insulin resistance by activating PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways and promoting GLUT4 translocation, highlighting its metabolic regulatory role.

top_papers.title: MRAP2a Binds and Modulates Activity and Localisation of Prokineticin Receptor 1 in Zebrafish.
top_papers.key_finding: MRAP2a interacts with zebrafish PROKR1, modulating its activity and localization, which affects downstream ERK and STAT3 signaling, suggesting regulatory mechanisms of PROKR1 function.

top_papers.title: PROKR1 delivery by cell-derived vesicles restores the myogenic potential of Prokr1-deficient C2C12 myoblasts.
top_papers.key_finding: Cell-derived vesicles enriched with PROKR1 can restore the myogenic potential of Prokr1-deficient C2C12 myoblasts, indicating a therapeutic approach involving PROKR1 for muscle regeneration.

top_papers.title: Prokineticins and their G protein-coupled receptors in health and disease.
top_papers.journal: Progress in molecular biology and translational science
top_papers.key_finding: PROKR1 is a key receptor mediating prokineticin signaling involved in diverse physiological functions and diseases, including angiogenesis, neurogenesis, and reproduction, with therapeutic potential.

top_papers.title: Application of a risk score model based on tyrosine-related genes in the prognosis and treatment of patients with lung adenocarcinoma.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 is included in a tyrosine-related gene risk score model for diagnosis and prognosis of lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting its potential as a biomarker though the study does not focus on its biological role.

top_papers.title: Prediction of Patients With High-Risk Osteosarcoma on the Basis of XGBoost Algorithm Using Transcriptome and Methylation Data From SGH-OS Cohort.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 is one of nine genes used in an XGBoost classifier to predict high-risk osteosarcoma subtypes, indicating its expression is relevant to disease classification but without detailed functional analysis.

top_papers.title: An eleven gene molecular signature for extra-capsular spread in oral squamous cell carcinoma serves as a prognosticator of outcome in patients without nodal metastases.
top_papers.key_finding: ZFP3 is part of an 11-gene molecular signature associated with extracapsular spread in oral squamous cell carcinoma, serving as a prognostic marker though the study does not explore its mechanistic role.

top_papers.title: The predictive value of plasma exosomal lncRNAs/mRNAs in NSCLC patients receiving immunotherapy.
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions lnc-ZFP3-3 as a long non-coding RNA trans-regulating certain mRNAs in NSCLC patients receiving immunotherapy, indicating a possible regulatory role but without direct study of the ZFP3 gene itself.

top_papers.title: Chromosomal localization of two human zinc finger protein genes, ZNF24 (KOX17) and ZNF29 (KOX26), to 18q12 and 17p13-p12, respectively.
top_papers.key_finding: Mentions the localization of ZFP3 gene on human chromosome 17p and its mouse homolog, indicating its chromosomal context but without functional or disease-related data.

functional_summary.original_summary: MED12 functions as a transcription coregulator that modulates the transcription of specific gene sets by interacting with DNA-binding transcription factors, often altering chromatin structure or facilitating transcriptional activation. Localization of MED12 to the nucleus and nucleoplasm is consistent with its role in regulating gene expression at the chromatin level.

gene_summary.original_summary: MED12 encodes a key subunit of the Mediator complex responsible for regulating transcription by RNA polymerase II. It engages with a network of 183 interaction partners, most notably MED13, MED6, MED24, CCNC, and MED22, and is annotated to the nucleoplasm. Expression of MED12 is highest in the ovary. MED12 causes a spectrum of developmental disorders including X-linked intellectual disability syndromes such as Lujan-Fryns syndrome and Hardikar syndrome, which can feature congenital diaphragmatic hernia and variable neurodevelopmental impairment. The literature on MED12 spans themes including intellectual disability linked to MED12 mutations, Mediator complex transcription regulation, and the broader phenotypic spectrum of MED12-related developmental disorders, with studies investigating variant effects on transcriptional control and chromatin modification.

It interacts with five partners, most notably PCDHA3, PCDHA10, PCDHA7, PCDHA2, and PCDHA8. PCDHA6 expression is highest in the brain, specifically in the cerebellar hemisphere and cerebellum. Expression of ZNF558 is highest in the uterus. Clinically, ZNF558 has been linked to neuronal development and psychiatric disorder genetics, with altered expression observed in neuronal cells impacting mitophagy and mitochondrial homeostasis; it is also implicated as a fusion partner in certain sarcomas. The literature on ZNF558 spans themes including gene regulatory networks, neuronal development, and structural genomic variation, with studies investigating its role in psychiatric disorder genetics.

gene_summary.original_summary: ZDBF2 encodes a zinc finger DBF-type containing protein involved primarily in the biological process of genomic imprinting. It has 42 known interaction partners, including key proteins such as SENP6, GPR1, and FAM50B. Expression of ZDBF2 is highest in the brain, specifically within the cerebellum and pituitary. Clinically, ZDBF2 mutations cause disorders such as Nasopalpebral Lipoma-coloboma syndrome, with evidence indicating pathogenicity from de novo heterozygous variants; it is also implicated in modulating cancer cell behaviors, including inhibition of ferroptosis and therapy resistance in oral squamous cell carcinoma. The literature on ZDBF2 spans themes including genomic imprinting regulation, epigenetic modification mechanisms, and cancer progression and therapy resistance, with recent studies investigating the roles of its circular RNA forms in transcriptional regulation and tumor biology.

functional_summary.original_summary: PREX1 functions as a guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor that stimulates the exchange of GDP for GTP on signaling GTPases, thereby activating them. It is involved in the positive regulation of cell migration and modulates actin filament polymerization, processes essential for cellular motility. Localization to the plasma membrane and cytosol suggests a role in transducing signals from membrane-associated receptors to cytoskeletal dynamics. Mechanistic detail beyond these activities is limited based on the provided annotations.

gene_summary.original_summary: SNRPN encodes the small nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide N, which functions primarily in mRNA splicing via the spliceosome. It has 248 known interaction partners, notably including SNRPD3, SNRPF, SNRPD1, SNRPD2, and SNRPG. Expression of SNRPN is highest in the brain, particularly in the cerebellar hemisphere. SNRPN causes neurodevelopmental defects through abnormal methylation and imprinting alterations, as seen in Prader-Willi syndrome, manifesting in impaired neuronal differentiation, reduced neural stem cell populations, and disrupted cortical and spine development. The literature on SNRPN spans themes including imprinting and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopment and neuronal function, and alternative splicing mechanisms, with recent studies investigating its role in rescuing neurodevelopmental impairment via regulatory interactions.

SNRPN causes neurodevelopmental defects through abnormal methylation and imprinting alterations, as seen in Prader-Willi syndrome, manifesting in impaired neuronal differentiation, reduced neural stem cell populations, and disrupted cortical and spine development. The literature on SNRPN spans themes including imprinting and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopment and neuronal function, and alternative splicing mechanisms, with recent studies investigating its role in rescuing neurodevelopmental impairment via regulatory interactions.

gene_summary.original_summary: CNP encodes 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide 3' phosphodiesterase, an enzyme involved in cyclic nucleotide catabolic processes and chemical synaptic transmission. It interacts with 105 partners, most notably MBP, GFAP, MAG, PLP1, and OLIG2, and is annotated to localise in the extracellular region, cytoplasm, and mitochondrion. Expression of CNP is highest in the spinal cord (cervical c-1) of the brain. CNP causes hypomyelinating leukodystrophy type 20 (HLD20), expanding the clinical spectrum of this neurological disorder characterized by defective myelination; genetic variants correlate with decreased CNP expression in patients. The literature on CNP spans themes including neurological disorders, cellular metabolism, and cardiovascular function, with studies investigating its structural features, functional roles, and potential as a therapeutic target.

gene_summary.original_summary: GYG2 encodes glycogenin 2, an enzyme that initiates glycogen biosynthesis by self-glucosylation to prime glycogen chains. It coordinates with 69 interaction partners, most notably glycogen synthases GYS1 and GYS2, glycogenin 1 (GYG1), 1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzyme (GBE1), and amylo-alpha-1,6-glucosidase (AGL); the protein localizes to the nucleus, cytoplasm, and cytosol. Expression of GYG2 is highest in subcutaneous adipose tissue. Clinically, GYG2 has been implicated in regulating glucose homeostasis and glycogen metabolism, with associations reported in cancer contexts such as glioma, where its expression relates to tumor growth and microenvironment features, and it also emerges as a biomarker linking mitochondrial function to aging processes in adipose tissue; these findings underline a phenotypic spectrum including metabolic and proliferative disorders. The literature on GYG2 spans themes including glycogen metabolism regulation, cancer biology, mitochondrial function and aging, with recent investigations focusing on its role in metabolic homeostasis and tumorigenesis.

gene_summary.original_summary: COL11A1 encodes the alpha 1 chain of type XI collagen, a structural protein involved in collagen fibril organization and skeletal system morphogenesis. It interacts with 158 partners, most prominently COL1A2, COL5A2, COL2A1, COL1A1, and COL3A1, and is annotated to extracellular regions and collagen trimers. Expression of COL11A1 is highest in cultured fibroblasts. Clinically, COL11A1 is strongly associated with hearing loss and Stickler syndrome as well as cancer progression, notably pancreatic and colorectal cancers, with implications for fibrosis and chemoresistance. The literature on COL11A1 spans themes including hearing loss and Stickler syndrome, cancer progression and therapy, and extracellular matrix remodeling, with studies investigating gene regulation and epigenetics.

gene_summary.original_summary: NDST4 encodes an enzyme with N-sulfotransferase activity involved in the biosynthesis of heparan sulfate proteoglycans. It coordinates with 39 partners, most notably HS2ST1, GLCE, and glypicans GPC5, GPC3, and GPC2. Expression of NDST4 is highest in nerve tissue, specifically in the tibial nerve. NDST4 has been identified as a candidate tumor suppressor gene with downregulation and allelic loss linked to colorectal cancer, where its altered function affects colonic epithelial cell differentiation and predicts adverse prognosis. The literature on NDST4 spans themes including heparan sulfate biosynthesis, cancer tumor suppression, and enzyme isoform characterization, with recent studies investigating its role in colonic epithelial differentiation.

gene_summary.original_summary: STS encodes steroid sulfatase, an enzyme essential for the catabolic process of steroid sulfates and involved in epidermis development. It interacts with 122 partners, notably including HSD3B1, AKR1C3, CYP17A1, HSD3B2, and SULT2B1, and is annotated to lysosome, endosome, and endoplasmic reticulum compartments. Expression of STS is highest in the artery tibial tissue. STS causes X-linked ichthyosis, a disorder characterized by scaling skin and often accompanied by neurological symptoms, with pathogenic deletions and mutations on Xp22.31 driving a broad phenotypic spectrum including contiguous gene syndromes. The literature on STS spans themes including X-linked ichthyosis genetics, neural precursor cell apoptosis, and steroid sulfatase inhibition, with studies investigating chromosomal variations and neurodevelopmental disorder mechanisms.

gene_summary.original_summary: TMEM163 encodes a transmembrane protein primarily involved in regulating intracellular zinc ion homeostasis, including zinc ion transmembrane transport and zinc ion import into synaptic vesicles. It interacts with six identified partners, most notably ACMSD, TMEM175, and CCDC62. Expression of TMEM163 is highest in the brain, specifically in the cerebellar hemisphere and cerebellum. Variants in TMEM163 cause a hypomyelinating leukodystrophy characterized by impaired zinc efflux, oligodendroglial dysfunction, and reduced myelin gene expression, leading to neurological deficits; TMEM163 deficiency also disrupts platelet dense granule biogenesis, implicating it in lysosome-related organelle function. The literature on TMEM163 spans themes including zinc transport and homeostasis, neurological disorders and hypomyelination, and metabolic disease associations, with recent studies investigating its role in protein interactions and cellular signalling.

gene_summary.original_summary: ZFP3 encodes a zinc finger protein involved in the regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. It has eight known protein interactions, with prominent partners including RCVRN, PTGER1, POLR2L, TP53, and SPARC, and is annotated to localize in the nucleus. Expression of ZFP3 is highest in the cerebellar hemisphere and cerebellum of the brain. Studies have identified ZFP3 as part of gene signatures relevant to cancer prognosis, including lung adenocarcinoma, osteosarcoma subtype classification, and oral squamous cell carcinoma, indicating its potential as a biomarker rather than a direct causative agent of disease. ZFP3 has been studied in the context of zinc finger protein genetics, chromosomal gene localization, transcriptional regulation in neural progenitor cells, Mediator complex function, and neurodevelopmental disorder mechanisms, with current research focusing on its role in transcriptional regulation and disease associations.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This gene set collectively highlights multiple distinct but interrelated biological processes relevant to MED12-related intellectual disability (ID) and Lujan-Fryns syndrome in neural progenitor cells (NPCs). A prominent cluster centers on transcriptional regulation and chromatin-associated mechanisms involving MED12 and several DNA-binding transcription factors (ZNF558, ZFP3, TCF7L2, SNRPN), supported by shared GO terms for nucleus localization and links to master regulators like TP53, ESR1, and AR. Another major theme involves membrane-associated proteins mediating cell adhesion and signaling (PCDHA3, PCDHA6, PCDHB5, PROKR1, STS, TMEM163) which may influence NPC connectivity or signaling pathways. Genes like F8A1, F8A2, F8A3, and CNP cluster around vesicle/endosomal transport and cytoskeletal dynamics, intersecting with neurodevelopmental processes. Several genes, especially non-coding RNAs (LINC00839, LINC02688), paralogs (HSD17B7P2), and poorly characterised genes (AKAP17A, DHRSX), lack functional overlap and may act via distinct or yet-undefined pathways. This diversity underscores the multifunctional molecular landscape through which MED12-associated pathology may arise, involving transcriptional dysregulation, cell adhesion, vesicle trafficking, and metabolism in NPCs.

KEY FINDINGS:
• **Mediator complex and transcriptional regulation cluster:** MED12, TCF7L2, ZFP3, ZNF558, and SNRPN share nucleus localization (GO:0005634) and protein binding (GO:0005515), with MED12 and TCF7L2 interacting with TP53, ESR1, AR, and CTCF, indicating coordinated regulation of gene expression and chromatin remodeling in NPCs underpinning MED12-dependent transcriptional dysregulation.
• **Neural cell adhesion and membrane proteins:** PCDHA3, PCDHA6, PCDHB5, PROKR1, STS, and TMEM163 share membrane and plasma membrane GO terms (GO:0016020, GO:0005886), mediating calcium-dependent homophilic adhesion and receptor signaling critical for NPC adhesion and communication relevant to neurodevelopment.
• **Vesicular transport and cytoskeletal dynamics:** F8A1, F8A2, F8A3, and CNP converge on cytoplasm and protein binding GO terms and share interaction partners like HTT, implicating them in endosomal transport and synaptic vesicle trafficking that may influence NPC function and neuronal connectivity.
• **Genes linked to ubiquitination and post-translational modifications:** TRIM61, a ubiquitin ligase, and RGPD1, involved in SUMOylation, indicate a layer of post-translational regulation potentially modulating protein stability and activity within NPCs, distinct from the core transcriptional or adhesion processes.
• **Metabolic and enzymatic function genes with tissue-specific expression:** ADPRHL1 (protein ADP-ribosylation removal), GYG2 (glycogen biosynthesis), PUDP (nucleotide metabolism), NDST4 (heparan sulfate sulfation), and STS (steroid desulfation) have enzymatic roles potentially affecting NPC metabolism or extracellular matrix remodeling, reflecting secondary pathways influencing MED12-related ID pathology.

network_overlap_analysis.interpretation: The interaction pattern suggests that MED12 serves as a central regulatory hub coordinating multiple signaling and transcriptional pathways in neural progenitor cells, consistent with its role in the Mediator complex. Its shared partners, including TP53, ESR1, AR, and PIK3CA, imply that MED12 may integrate signals related to cell cycle control, hormone response, and PI3K/AKT signaling to modulate gene expression programs critical for neurodevelopment. The direct interactions among F8A family members indicate a tightly coordinated subnetwork potentially involved in vesicular trafficking or coagulation-related processes that might indirectly impact NPC function or maintenance. Additionally, the clustering of protocadherin interactions (e.g., PCDHA3 and PCDHA6) points towards coordinated regulation of cell adhesion and neuronal connectivity. The presence of interactions with imprinted genes like SNRPN and associated partners suggests epigenetic regulation layers contributing to the observed network, which may influence neurodevelopmental phenotypes linked to MED12 dysfunction. Collectively, these patterns underscore a multifaceted mechanism where MED12 orchestrates diverse pathways through both direct and shared interactions, supporting its hypothesized contribution to intellectual disability via transcriptional dysregulation in neural progenitors.

cross_gene_synthesis.original_summary:
• **Mediator complex and transcriptional regulation cluster:** MED12, TCF7L2, ZFP3, ZNF558, and SNRPN share nucleus localization (GO:0005634) and protein binding (GO:0005515), with MED12 and TCF7L2 interacting with TP53, ESR1, AR, and CTCF, indicating coordinated regulation of gene expression and chromatin remodeling in NPCs underpinning MED12-dependent transcriptional dysregulation.
• **Neural cell adhesion and membrane proteins:** PCDHA3, PCDHA6, PCDHB5, PROKR1, STS, and TMEM163 share membrane and plasma membrane GO terms (GO:0016020, GO:0005886), mediating calcium-dependent homophilic adhesion and receptor signaling critical for NPC adhesion and communication relevant to neurodevelopment.
